plain.text: Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming with four hundred men. He arranged his family and went ahead of them, bowing to the ground seven times as he approached. But Esau ran to meet Jacob, embraced him, threw his arms around his neck and kissed him, and they wept. Esau asked about the women and children, and they bowed to him. Esau did not want to take the gifts, saying, "I already have plenty." Jacob insisted: "To see your face is like seeing the face of God, now that you have received me favourably." Esau offered to travel with him, but Jacob said the children and animals needed to go slowly. Esau went back to Seir, and Jacob went to Sukkoth and built shelters for his livestock.
Jacob arrived safely at the city of Shechem in Canaan. He bought a piece of land, set up an altar there, and called it El-Elohe-Israel ("God, the God of Israel").

summary.bigIdea: After twenty years, Esau runs to meet Jacob and embraces him, and the brothers are reconciled.
points: Jacob approaches Esau humbly, bowing seven times.
Esau runs, embraces and kisses him, and they weep together.
Jacob says seeing Esau's face is like seeing the face of God.
summary.reflection: Esau ran to embrace the brother who had wronged him. Is there a relationship where you long for reconciliation?
